messages.content: You are BioGPT, an expert compiler architect. Translate the provided natural language biological protocol into valid, deterministic BioScript code for execution on a microfluidic biochip.

Source link: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3079775/pdf/nihms263296.pdf
Paper DOI: https://doi.org/10.1002/biot.201000324

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Picoliter-Scale Electrowetting Digital Microfluidic Pyrosequencing (Bead-Bound DNA Extension Coupled to ATP-Sulfurylase/Luciferase Chemiluminescent Detection)

REAGENTS USED:
  - DNA-Bound Paramagnetic Beads (target DNA template bound to streptavidin-functionalized paramagnetic beads, magnetically held at the reservoir exit)
  - Polymerase (DNA polymerase used to catalyze template-directed nucleotide incorporation)
  - dNTP (single deoxynucleotide triphosphate, e.g. dATP, cyclically dispensed one base at a time during sequencing-by-synthesis)
  - APS (adenosine 5'-phosphosulfate, substrate for ATP sulfurylase)
  - ATP Sulfurylase (enzyme converting released pyrophosphate + APS into ATP)
  - Luciferin (D-luciferin substrate for firefly luciferase, 400 ug/mL working concentration)
  - Luciferase (QuantiLum recombinant firefly luciferase, 1.0-2.0 ug/uL working concentration for optimal picoliter-scale signal)
  - Wash Buffer (50 mM TRIS pH 7.6, 5.0 mM magnesium acetate, 0.5 mM EDTA, 1.0 mM DTT, 0.01-0.02% wt Tween 20, used to rinse beads between cycles and prevent cross-contamination)

STEPS:
1. Bead loading: Dispense the DNA-bound paramagnetic bead droplet and a polymerase droplet, magnetically hold the beads at the reservoir exit, and mix to form the primed template droplet.
2-5. Nucleotide addition (repeated once per base in the sequencing cycle): Dispense a single dNTP droplet and mix it with the bead-bound template so that, per Equation 1 (DNA + dNTP --Polymerase--> DNA-dNP + PPi), a correct incorporation releases pyrophosphate (PPi) into the droplet.
6. ATP generation: Dispense APS and ATP sulfurylase droplets and sequentially mix them with the extension droplet so that, per Equation 2 (PPi + APS --ATP Sulfurylase--> ATP + SO4^2-), the released PPi is converted to ATP.
7. Chemiluminescent detection: Dispense luciferin and luciferase droplets and sequentially mix them with the ATP-containing droplet so that, per Equation 3 (ATP + Luciferin + O2 --Luciferase--> AMP + PPi + Oxyluciferin + CO2 + Light), light is produced in proportion to the amount of ATP (and therefore the number of bases incorporated); observe/quantify the resulting chemiluminescence intensity with a cooled CCD camera over a fixed exposure window.
8. Signal evaluation and bead rinse: If the detected intensity falls below the empirically determined limit-of-detection threshold (~7 nM ATP equivalent, S/N = 5), dispose of the reacted droplet and re-form the bead-bound template by mixing the magnetically-held beads with a fresh wash-buffer droplet before the next cycle, to eliminate dilution/cross-contamination effects; otherwise carry the reacted droplet forward as the template for the next nucleotide-addition cycle.
9. Cycle repeat: Repeat steps 2-8 for each subsequent base in the sequencing run.
10. Final rinse and disposal: After the sequencing cycles are complete, rinse the bead-bound template with successive wash-buffer droplets to remove residual reagent, then discard.

INTERPRETATION: Successful pyrosequencing chemistry on the picoliter-scale device is confirmed by a linear chemiluminescence response to ATP concentration (limit of detection ~7 nM ATP, corresponding to single-nucleotide incorporation on ~2 amol of DNA in a 300 pL droplet) and by luciferase-concentration optimization (1.0-2.0 ug/uL) yielding sufficient initial peak intensity for reliable detection despite the inherently lower light output at picoliter droplet volumes, supporting the feasibility of miniaturized digital-microfluidic pyrosequencing for low-reagent-volume, field-portable DNA sequencing.

module fluorescence

manifest DNA_Beads
manifest Polymerase
manifest dATP
manifest APS
manifest ATP_Sulfurylase
manifest Luciferin
manifest Luciferase
manifest Wash_Buffer

instructions:

beads = dispense 1 units of DNA_Beads
poly = dispense 5 units of Polymerase
template = mix beads with poly for 10s

repeat 4 times {

    // --- nucleotide addition: DNA + dNTP --Polymerase--> DNA-dNP + PPi ---
    nucleotide = dispense 5 units of dATP
    template = mix template with nucleotide for 10s

    // --- PPi + APS --ATP Sulfurylase--> ATP + SO4(2-) ---
    aps = dispense 5 units of APS
    sulfurylase = dispense 5 units of ATP_Sulfurylase
    template = mix template with aps for 10s
    template = mix template with sulfurylase for 10s

    // --- ATP + Luciferin + O2 --Luciferase--> AMP + PPi + Oxyluciferin + CO2 + Light ---
    luc_substrate = dispense 5 units of Luciferin
    luc_enzyme = dispense 5 units of Luciferase
    template = mix template with luc_substrate for 5s
    template = mix template with luc_enzyme for 5s

    signal = detect fluorescence on template for 10s

    if (signal < 7) {
        dispose template
        wash = dispense 300 units of Wash_Buffer
        template = mix beads with wash for 5s
    }
}

// --- final wash / rinse cycle before disposal ---
repeat 2 times {
    rinse = dispense 300 units of Wash_Buffer
    template = mix template with rinse for 5s
}

dispose template

ir.content:
main:
	beads1[0] = dispense(DNA_Beads)
	poly1[0] = dispense(Polymerase)
	template1[0] = mix(beads1[0], poly1[0]) @ 10.0SECOND
bsbbr_2_h:
	PHI REPEAT_41 = {REPEAT_40,REPEAT_42}
	PHI wash1 = {wash0,wash3}
	PHI aps1 = {aps0,aps2}
	PHI sulfurylase1 = {sulfurylase0,sulfurylase2}
	PHI luc_enzyme1 = {luc_enzyme0,luc_enzyme2}
	PHI luc_substrate1 = {luc_substrate0,luc_substrate2}
	PHI nucleotide1 = {nucleotide0,nucleotide2}
	PHI signal1 = {signal0,signal2}
	PHI template2 = {template1,template9}
	if REPEAT_41[0] > 0	|	true: jump bsbbr_3_t	|	false: jump bsbbr_6_f
bsbbr_3_t:
	nucleotide2[0] = dispense(dATP)
	template3[0] = mix(template2[0], nucleotide2[0]) @ 10.0SECOND
	aps2[0] = dispense(APS)
	sulfurylase2[0] = dispense(ATP_Sulfurylase)
	template4[0] = mix(template3[0], aps2[0]) @ 10.0SECOND
	template5[0] = mix(template4[0], sulfurylase2[0]) @ 10.0SECOND
	luc_substrate2[0] = dispense(Luciferin)
	luc_enzyme2[0] = dispense(Luciferase)
	template6[0] = mix(template5[0], luc_substrate2[0]) @ 5.0SECOND
	template7[0] = mix(template6[0], luc_enzyme2[0]) @ 5.0SECOND
	signal2[0] = detect(fluorescence, template7[0]) @ 10.0SECOND
	if signal2[0] < 7	|	true: jump bsbbif_4_t	|	false: jump bsbbif_5_f
bsbbif_4_t:
	dispose(template7[0])
	wash2[0] = dispense(Wash_Buffer)
	template8[0] = mix(beads1[0], wash2[0]) @ 5.0SECOND
bsbbif_5_f:
	PHI wash3 = {wash1,wash2}
	PHI template9 = {template7,template8}
	REPEAT_42[0] = REPEAT_41[0] - 1
	jump: bsbbr_2_h
bsbbr_6_f:
bsbbr_7_h:
	PHI rinse1 = {rinse0,rinse2}
	PHI REPEAT_21 = {REPEAT_20,REPEAT_22}
	PHI template10 = {template2,template11}
	if REPEAT_21[0] > 0	|	true: jump bsbbr_8_t	|	false: jump bsbbr_9_f
bsbbr_8_t:
	rinse2[0] = dispense(Wash_Buffer)
	template11[0] = mix(template10[0], rinse2[0]) @ 5.0SECOND
	REPEAT_22[0] = REPEAT_21[0] - 1
bsbbr_9_f:
	dispose(template10[0])
	NOP

chemical_evidence.source_quote: Bead-bound DNA is magnetically held in a single location, and wash or reagent droplets added or split from it
The released pyrophosphate is then converted to adenosine triphosphate (ATP) via a reaction with adenosine 5'-phosphosulfate (APS) and ATP sulfurylase
the substrate solution consisted of 400 ug/mL luciferin ... the enzyme solution contained the specified concentration of luciferase
reagents can be added and excess split away without loss of the DNA ... The DNA beads can also be rinsed with a few successive droplets of buffer to prevent cross-contamination

operation_evidence.bs_operation: template = mix template with nucleotide for 10s
operation_evidence.source_quote: The nucleotides are individually added to a primed template strand and cycled as the sequencing progresses

operation_evidence.bs_operation: template = mix template with aps for 10s / template = mix template with sulfurylase for 10s
operation_evidence.source_quote: The released pyrophosphate is then converted to adenosine triphosphate (ATP) via a reaction with adenosine 5'-phosphosulfate (APS) and ATP sulfurylase

operation_evidence.bs_operation: template = mix template with luc_substrate for 5s / template = mix template with luc_enzyme for 5s
operation_evidence.source_quote: after which the ATP will react with firefly luciferase, luciferin and oxygen to produce light

operation_evidence.bs_operation: signal = detect fluorescence on template for 10s
operation_evidence.source_quote: Camera settings were 8x8 pixel binning, and 10 s exposure time. All reactions were started precisely at the beginning of the 10 s window

operation_evidence.bs_operation: if (signal < 7) { dispose template; wash = dispense 300 units of Wash_Buffer; template = mix beads with wash for 5s }
operation_evidence.source_quote: the limit of detection for these circumstances was calculated to be 7 nM ATP (S/N=5)

operation_evidence.bs_operation: repeat 2 times { rinse = dispense 300 units of Wash_Buffer; template = mix template with rinse for 5s }
operation_evidence.source_quote: The DNA beads can also be rinsed with a few successive droplets of buffer to prevent cross-contamination

numeric_mismatches.note: The paper cycles through all four natural nucleotides (A/C/G/T) sequentially during pyrosequencing-by-synthesis; BioScript cannot iterate over a heterogeneous reagent list, so a single re-dispensed dATP manifest stands in for one generic base-addition cycle repeated 4 times, rather than four explicitly distinct per-base branches.

The paper's 7 nM ATP limit-of-detection (S/N=5, Section 3.3.3) is used as a proxy numeric threshold for the detect() intensity comparison; the paper does not itself define a control-flow branch on this value, since the reported experiments (Figures 7-8) characterize detection limits and luciferase optimization independently rather than as part of a live sequencing decision loop.

numeric_mismatches.field: template = mix beads with wash for 5s (rewash branch)
numeric_mismatches.note: The paper describes magnetic bead-holding and buffer rinsing qualitatively (Section 1, Section 3.2) but does not report an explicit droplet-level rewash timing; 5s is an illustrative duration consistent with the paper's other short mixing/incubation steps, not a literal reported value.

numeric_mismatches.field: magnetic bead-well manipulation (Section 3.2, Figures 4-6) and bead-count dispensing statistics (Section 3.1, Figure 3)
numeric_mismatches.note: Not modeled. These are device-characterization/simulation experiments (COMSOL magnet-geometry optimization, bead-per-droplet statistics) rather than steps of the core sequencing chemistry itself, and BioScript's grammar exposes no magnetic-hold or bead-counting primitive, so they fall outside the scope of this translation.
